rationale: Three sensors (door_back, motion_living, win_bed) dropped within the same second (14:02:00–14:02:02) while the base station and all cameras remain online, and their batteries are healthy (81/74/66%), ruling out battery drain. The base station log shows E-610 "radio module self-test warning" with normal RSSI history (-55 to -66 dBm), and the KB/historical case H-05 confirm this exact pattern indicates a base-station radio module fault requiring FAE escalation.

output.symptom_summary: Three sensors (Back Door, Living Motion, Bedroom Window) went offline simultaneously at 14:02:00-14:02:02 while base station and cameras remained online. Batteries are healthy (81%, 74%, 66%).
output.suspected_root_cause: Base station sub-GHz radio module fault (E-610 self-test warning) causing batch link failure.

output.customer_reply: Thanks for your patience. We've identified a hardware issue with your base station's radio module, not the sensor batteries. Our engineering team will contact you within 24 hours to arrange a replacement. No need to order batteries.

results.text: Logged by the base station when its sub-GHz radio fails self-test or multiple peripherals drop simultaneously. Always escalate to FAE.

The peripheral firmware speaks a radio protocol the base station no longer supports, or vice versa. Frontline action: trigger OTA upgrade of the peripheral. If OTA is not available for the device or fails twice, escalate to FAE as protocol conflict.

results.text: Three sensors in different rooms went offline at the same minute; base station online, RSSI history normal, E-610 in log. Restarting did not help. Escalated; radio module replaced. Escalated correctly.

complaint: Three of my sensors went offline at the same time this afternoon. I got three offline notifications within a few seconds of each other. The front camera is still fine. I assumed the batteries had run low because they are the originals from 18 months ago, so I'm about to order a bunch of new ones. Is that the right call?
